payload.headline: AMD slips 1.75% to 406.03, sitting on support, still above fair value

summary.thesis: AMD is growing faster and earning more, but at 406.03 the price assumes 51.8% yearly cash-flow growth, well above every fair-value estimate in our data.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for 333.38 or lower. Swing: no trade while the downtrend holds.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy case starts at 333.38; swing only after a close above 451.0

payload.happening: AMD fell 1.75% to 406.03. That puts it just above the 391.92–403.54 support zone and below its 20-day (489.22), 50-day (548.35) and 200-day (432.96) averages, so the trend is down. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
payload.business: The business itself is getting stronger. Sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, up from 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, reached 7.1B over the last twelve months, up from 5.4B. The company holds 8.7B more cash than debt, so its finances are not at risk. Analysts raised next-year earnings estimates by 11.3% in 30 days. Two things are at risk. First, inventory rose 57% while quarterly sales rose 45% (both against a year earlier). Unsold chips can force price cuts, and that would hit margins. Second, the 18% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range of -2% to 22%, and margins this high often come back down. The recent price drop looks like a change in mood, not in the business: the tech market is in a downtrend, and put open interest is 2.41 times call interest. Nothing in the latest filing shows demand weakening.

worth.text: At 406.03, AMD trades at 88.5 times last year's earnings, 23.0 times next year's expected earnings, and 14.7 times sales. The peer median is 12.3 times sales, and AMD's own price-to-sales ratio is in the 88th percentile of its last five years. A cash-flow model (DCF), which values today's free cash flow of 7.1B grown over time, gives 147.69 to 225.08, with 189.77 in the middle. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. To justify today's price, cash flow would need to start growing at 51.8% a year. The model caps starting growth at 30%, and even at that cap the value is only 189.77. The gap between the two views comes down to one question: does analysts' 118% next-year EPS growth last, or fade like normal growth? Margins matter too. If operating margin fell back to 13%, the model value drops to 100.01.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the price implies 51.8% a year while the model caps it at 30%, so the price only makes sense if the 118% jump in next-year EPS growth keeps going.

bull: Growth is speeding up: quarterly sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, up from 37.85% two quarters ago.
Profitability nearly doubled: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow climbed to 7.1B from 5.4B.
Estimates are rising fast: next-year EPS of 17.64 was raised 11.3% in 30 days, which puts the stock at 23.0 times next year's earnings.
bear: The price needs 51.8% starting cash-flow growth. Even at the model's 30% cap, the value is 189.77, far below 406.03.
Inventory rose 57% against 45% sales growth. If that leads to price cuts and operating margin falls to 13%, the model value drops to 100.01.
The stock costs 14.7 times sales, above the peer median of 12.3 and in the 88th percentile of its own 5-year range.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 391.92–403.54 support zone. A close below it would point to the next zone at 347.18–358.8, and the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range, based on AMD's own price-to-sales history. The value case for buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business is strong and improving, but the price assumes far more growth than any method supports. Wait for 333.38 or lower, or for results that support much faster lasting growth.

swing.why: The trend is down: lower highs and lower lows, and the price is below all three averages. The average daily range (ATR) of 46.51 is wider than the whole 391.92–403.54 support zone, so a stop there would sit inside normal daily swings. No trade until a close above 451.0, the top of the 424.03–451.0 resistance zone.

decision.timing: The 2027-02-02 report is more than two months away. Options price an 18.6% move by 2026-12-18, and the most put open interest sits at the 400 strike, so mood alone could push the price below the support zone before the report.

change_mind: A price at or below 333.38 would bring AMD into its fair-value range and would turn the long-term action toward buy.
In the 2027-02-02 report, a beat of the 3.3 next-quarter EPS estimate together with inventory growth falling back below sales growth (now 57% vs 45%) would ease the margin risk.
A close above 451.0 would break the 424.03–451.0 resistance and end the swing no-trade stance. A close below 391.92 would confirm the selloff toward 347.18–358.8.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait and no trade, because the price fell 1.75% to 406.03 and remains above the 333.38 top of the fair-value range.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
